:::{#exm-interaction}
#### A linear predictor with an interaction term

Suppose a model has a numeric covariate $x$, a binary covariate $z \in \{0, 1\}$,
and linear predictor

$$\eta(x, z) = 1 + 2x + 3z + 4xz.$$

The difference in $\eta$ per unit difference in $x$, holding $z$ fixed, is:

$$
\ba
\eta(x + 1, z) - \eta(x, z)
&= \sb{1 + 2(x + 1) + 3z + 4(x + 1)z} - \sb{1 + 2x + 3z + 4xz}
&& \text{(substitute into } \eta\text{)}
\\
&= \sb{1 + 2x + 2 + 3z + 4xz + 4z} - \sb{1 + 2x + 3z + 4xz}
&& \text{(distribute)}
\\
&= 2 + 4z
&& \text{(cancel shared terms)}
\ea
$$

- When $z = 0$: the difference is $2 + 4 \cdot 0 = 2$.
- When $z = 1$: the difference is $2 + 4 \cdot 1 = 6$.

The difference per unit of $x$ depends on $z$,
so this model includes an interaction between $x$ and $z$,
and $4xz$ is its interaction term,
with interaction coefficient $4$.
:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-no-interaction}
#### A linear predictor without an interaction term (counterexample)

Now drop the interaction term, so that $\eta(x, z) = 1 + 2x + 3z$.
Then:

$$
\ba
\eta(x + 1, z) - \eta(x, z)
&= \sb{1 + 2(x + 1) + 3z} - \sb{1 + 2x + 3z}
&& \text{(substitute into } \eta\text{)}
\\
&= \sb{1 + 2x + 2 + 3z} - \sb{1 + 2x + 3z}
&& \text{(distribute)}
\\
&= 2
&& \text{(cancel shared terms)}
\ea
$$

The difference per unit of $x$ is $2$ at both $z = 0$ and $z = 1$,
so this model has no interaction between $x$ and $z$:
the lines for $z = 0$ and $z = 1$ are parallel on the scale of $\eta$.
:::
